description: ChangesResponse adds BOTH a typed Option<Vec<String>> field `updated_properties` (renamed "updatedProperties") AND a flatten `extra` field. Probe needed: if a server returns `{ ..., "updatedProperties": null, "acmeCustom": 1 }`, does `extra` catch only `acmeCustom` or also intercept the explicit `null` of `updatedProperties` somehow? Per serde docs, flatten visits remaining keys AFTER named fields are consumed, and null-valued keys for Option<T> fields are consumed by the named field. So this should be fine. But there's no test pinning the interaction. The methods.rs test `changes_response_accepts_explicit_null_updated_properties` proves `updated_properties: null` deserializes as None, and `changes_response_preserves_vendor_extras` proves an unknown field lands in extra. NOT TESTED: BOTH together. Recommendation: add a single test that combines an explicit null updatedProperties + a vendor extra + an unknown sub-field, to pin the interaction so a future serde change doesn't silently break it. Probe-deferred per read-only review.
title: extra field flatten + ChangesResponse.updated_properties unflatten ordering risk
